items.title: Turn coordinated enemy formations into bounded observed after-action evidence and formation-specific revenge drills.
items.why: getSpawnFormationPlan and applySpawnFormation already stamp formation identity, lane, and role on live enemies, but pressure-arc-v1 persists only pressure bands. DeathScreen therefore cannot distinguish a pincer, escort, flank, or surge exposure, even though formation tactics are a meaningful late-wave mastery signal.
items.recipe: Upgrade the pressure receipt to a backward-compatible v2 formation ledger. Record only transitions/exposure counts from actual spawn plans, preserve a bounded chronological sample, and derive a dominant observed formation plus literal counterplay copy. Feed the receipt through deathFlow/run history and DeathScreen using OBSERVED FORMATION language, never cause-of-death language. Add invalid-input, cap, tie, backward-compatibility, description, and UI fixtures; expose the vocabulary in the public gameplay contract if the generator supports source-derived mechanics.

L1.recipe: Persist formation exposure counts in the existing pressure receipt and add a literal DeathScreen line.

L2.recipe: Add bounded transition evidence, dominant-formation derivation, counterplay vocabulary, and focused model/UI tests.

L3.recipe: Ship a backward-compatible observed-formation contract across runtime, death flow, run history, public gameplay truth, telemetry, and fail-closed fixtures.

items.axis: speed / architecture / replay integrity / token reduction
items.title: Replace the long-run ghost array shift cliff with an extracted fixed-capacity chronological recorder.
items.why: App records one ghost sample every six frames, caps the array at 18000, and then calls shift() on every additional sample. That is an O(n) hot-path operation during long runs, while reset, terminal marking, serialization, and capacity semantics remain inline in the 5000-line orchestrator.
items.recipe: Create a pure fixed-capacity recorder with O(1) append/overwrite, finite integer normalization, chronological export, terminal-sample annotation, explicit capacity/count/overwrites receipt, and safe hydration of prior arrays. Replace App's array lifecycle without changing sessionStorage wire format or ghost playback behavior. Add wraparound, exact-cap, invalid-sample, terminal-update, reset, and serialization parity tests; ratchet the architecture receipt after the extraction.

L1.recipe: Extract append/cap/export helpers while retaining an array implementation.

L2.recipe: Implement the circular recorder and preserve chronological storage/playback compatibility with focused tests.

L3.recipe: Ship the recorder, lifecycle integration, integrity receipt, malformed-input handling, App architecture ratchet, and exact behavior fixtures.

items.title: Make guest boot and front-door controls fail open when local or session storage is denied.
items.why: App and HomeV2 directly call localStorage/sessionStorage during state initialization and click handlers. The repository already classifies quota, security, and unavailable storage failures, but those direct calls can throw before or outside the recovery surface, contradicting the instant guest-play promise.
items.recipe: Add one typed safe-browser-storage adapter for get/set/remove/JSON operations that never throws, preserves default values, and reports sanitized per-surface failures through the existing storage-health receipt. Migrate boot-critical App and HomeV2 preference/dismissal/debug paths plus ghost session hydration/persistence. Add throwing-storage fixtures, unavailable-global fixtures, JSON corruption fixtures, recovery tests, and an App/Home boot smoke proving the deploy surface remains usable without storage.

L1.recipe: Wrap boot-time reads in try/catch defaults and add a denied-storage smoke.

L2.recipe: Create a shared adapter, migrate entry reads/writes, and reuse the storage-health classifier.

L3.recipe: Ship the unified adapter, boot/front-door/ghost integration, sanitized receipts, fail-open UI behavior, and browser-storage denial fixtures.

skipped.reason: No participant or production distribution supports changing damage, health, spawn, cooldown, reward, or progression values.
The deterministic local intelligence stack is deep; a hosted model adds variable per-user cost and weaker evidence discipline without a demonstrated player need.
Guest play is intentional and membership remains an explicit product decision rather than a defect.
Production Lighthouse and funnel evidence remain absent; the existing evidence gate still applies.
The analytics capability remains missing and the available Sentry DSN is not proven project-scoped.
Brevo readiness does not prove delivery; the end-to-end policy/tool gap remains routed through Ark.
Automation cannot replace a physical PWA/gamepad/full-run pass or direct image judgment.
The game already has substantial modes, builds, bosses, missions, rivals, replay, and meta progression. More raw content ranks below closing live loop/resilience gaps.
